_comment: The numbers, and what the price implies. Read when financial quality or valuation actually matters - not every day. Fill what research established; leave the rest null. A null is information, an invented figure is corruption.

summary._supports_note: Does the business evidence actually back the market narrative, or is the story running ahead of the numbers?

core_metrics._note: The small set that usually decides the judgment. Anything else worth noting goes in other_metrics rather than expanding this list.
core_metrics._deducted_note: 扣非归母净利润 - often the more honest profit number

_other_metrics_note: Free-form. Add only figures that matter for this particular company - ROE, inventory, goodwill, receivables, order book, capacity. Do not pre-populate.

quality_checks._note: Only fill what is actually a concern for this company. Leave the rest empty rather than writing 'no issue' everywhere.

concept_exposure._verdict_options: real beneficiary | partial exposure | proxy/concept stock | unclear
concept_exposure._note: This is the evidence behind real_or_proxy in stock_profile.json. Keep the two consistent.

valuation._basis_note: How the judgment was reached - peer multiple, historical range, earnings power. Prefer a practical range over fake precision; avoid DCF unless the business is stable and it is genuinely needed.

refresh_control._triggers_note: EXCEPTIONS ONLY. Standard triggers (new report, guidance, rerating, concept-exposure change, balance-sheet or shareholder risk event) apply to every stock and live in stock_profiles_readme.md.

digest_for_stock_profile._note: One or two lines, copied into financial_digest in stock_profile.json whenever this file changes, so the cover page never contradicts the file beneath it.
